articles.headline: Electric vehicle sales in the U.S. are showing signs of life
keyFacts: U.S. electric vehicle sales grew for three consecutive quarters and captured 6.1 percent of the market, according to a Cox Automotive report.
Cox Automotive director Stephanie Valdez Streaty said competitive EV prices and high gas prices sparked renewed consumer interest.
Toyota, Rivian, and Subaru led the sales growth, while Tesla saw its sales drop by 20 percent year-over-year.
body: Don’t go writing the obituary for the U.S. electric vehicle just yet. After sales tanked following the cancellation of tax credits last year, they’ve been growing for the last three consecutive quarters, according to a new report from Cox Automotive.

EV’s captured 6.1% of the U.S. market, their best showing since the third quarter of 2025. The data shows that the EV market is “finding its footing again,” Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive, said in an analysis that accompanied the new report. EV prices have become more competitive, and high gas prices have sparked renewed consumer interest, she added.

Toyota, Rivian, and Subaru led the pack. Sales of the Toyota bZ and Lexus RZ about doubled following a refresh that hit dealerships late last year. The updated models adopted Tesla-style charging ports and received larger batteries, more powerful motors, and faster charging times.
Meanwhile, Tesla’s sales dropped by 20% year-over-year. Tesla still retains the first-mover advantage, though, selling over half of all EVs during the third quarter.

The recovery in the U.S. mimics what occurred in Germany after the government stopped incentives for EV purchases in November 2023, a year earlier than expected. The following month, sales fell by more than half. But after hitting that low, the market steadily recovered. German EV sales in August, the most recent month for which data is available, were the second highest on record.

articles.headline: NASA explains how it's making batteries for the Moon's extreme temperatures
keyFacts: NASA shared details about the SPEARS project developing batteries that can withstand extreme temperatures on the Moon.
Traditional lithium-ion batteries fail on the Moon because daytime highs reach 212 degrees Fahrenheit and nighttime lows drop to minus 328 degrees Fahrenheit.
The SPEARS project uses solid ceramic or polymer materials instead of liquid electrolytes to prevent damage from extreme cold.
body: NASA explains how it's making batteries for the Moon's extreme temperatures
The SPEARS project’s work could be used during future Artemis missions.

NASA often has fascinating science happening behind the scenes of its astronomical endeavors. Today, the space agency shared some details about a project to create batteries capable of withstanding extreme cold. The eventual goal is to use them for campaigns on the Moon, such as the future Artemis missions.

The lithium-ion batteries that power most electronics here on Earth are based on liquid electrolytes which can freeze at low temperatures, damaging the battery. And as you may have learned first-hand when your phone powers itself off in an overheated car, these types of batteries also won't work at very high temperatures. The moon can hit daytime highs of 212 degrees F (100 degrees C) while the nighttime lows at its southern pole plummet to as low as minus 328 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 200 Celsius), meaning current battery tech won't cut it.

Solid Power for Extreme Environment Adaptability and Resilience in Space, or SPEARS, has been a project for developing a battery with a solid ceramic or polymer material instead of the liquid. These alternative batteries still need to be warmed up to function, but thus far they haven't been damaged by extreme cold and they require less energy-intensive thermal management systems than their lithium-ion counterparts.

The whole NASA blog post is well worth a read for any space and/or science nerds. While the team is developing the batteries for the dramatic climates of Mars, it's possible the same technology could one day power gadgets here on Earth too.

articles.headline: Texans confirm Marvin Harrison’s status for Week 6
keyFacts: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed that wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will play against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 6.
Ryans stated that Harrison will have a limited role and will not play every snap as he learns the offensive system.

Marvin Harrison Jr. will play against Jaguars, but Texans plan limited role

Former Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (18). Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans has confirmed that Marvin Harrison Jr. will play against Jacksonville in Week 6, according to Aaron Wilson (h/t Aaron Wilson).
“Marvin will play,” Ryans said.

However, the former Arizona Cardinals receiver should not be expected to play every snap as he settles into Houston’s offensive system. Ryans explained that the coaching staff will focus on what Harrison can comfortably learn and execute.

“What is he able to pick up on? We’ll make sure it’s as easy as possible for him. Don’t expect him to play all 60 snaps. Make sure he has what he needs and he’s confident in what we need him to do,” Ryans said, per Wilson.
Harrison reunites with Stroud, his former Ohio State teammate, after Houston acquired him from Arizona. The Texans will ease him into the offense rather than force an immediate, full workload.

Following Katie Zacharia’s debut press briefing on Tuesday, we’ve been spending more time digging into her background.

Zacharia was relatively unknown when Trump announced her selection to be his next press secretary last week, after the departure of Karoline Leavitt earlier this year. In the days since, several outlets have uncovered a series of since-deleted social media posts that promote debunked or baseless conspiracies.
In a series of now-scrubbed posts on X, reviewed by the Guardian, Zacharia fawned over Tesla and Space X founder, Elon Musk.

On 22 May 2022, the new press secretary described Musk, a tech billionaire and Trump ally, as “based”. She went on to explain the term was applied “when you want to recognize someone for being themselves” and “courageous and unique or not caring what others think”.

In another post from the same year, Zacharia also responded to one user sharing a widely circulated picture of Musk and Ghislaine Maxwell, the co-conspirator of the late sex-offender Jeffrey Epstein, at the Vanity Fair Oscar party in 2014, where Zacharia wrote “oh please, he already responded to this post. #oldnews”.
Musk has not been charged with any wrongdoing in connection with Epstein, and has denied knowing Maxwell, claiming the photo which pictures her standing close to him is because she “photobombed” him.

In other now-deleted posts, also from the same period, Zacharia directed various complimentary messages at Musk. “#IstandwithElon,” she wrote in one. In another she praised him for renouncing his support for the Democratic party and saying he would now support Republicans. “Smartest and richest man in the world right here is saying out loud what everyone else is thinking,” Zacharia wrote.
However, last year Zacharia questioned whether Musk could have been trusted “from the beginning” while appearing as a guest on conservative commentator Buck Sexton’s podcast.

Meanwhile, CNN also found now-deleted social media posts where Zacharia wrote and reshared comments that accused prominent political figures and Hollywood elites of pedophilia. Ken Paxton says Greg Abbott is 'struggling' in Texas gubernatorial race in leaked audio – report

In leaked audio obtained by Rolling Stone, Ken Paxton – the Republican nominee for US Senate in Texas – said that Greg Abbott – the incumbent GOP governor – was “struggling” in his re-election bid against Democratic state legislator Gina Hinojosa.

“Yes, Abbott is struggling, but he has a lot of money. [Hinojosa] has none,” Paxton told attenders at a private donor event in Washington DC, according to Rolling Stone. Paxton said that even though Hinojosa has “no name ID” the race is “still close”.
He added: “[Abbott] didn’t have any primary, like I did, that was brutal with all the negative ads.”

This is the latest audio leak from the 24 September event, where Paxton appears to have justified his extremely competitive race, in which he’s trailing in the polls against his Democratic opponent, James Talarico.

In a 30-page order issued on Tuesday, Jesse M Furman, a judge at the US district court for the southern district of New York, granted a preliminary injunction to the two groups, Democracy for the Arab World Now (Dawn) and Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide (Taag).

The order warned the US government would “impose tangible and significant consequences” on people involved in investigations that Washington said threatened the national security of the US or its allies, including Israel.

The order came after the ICC issued arrest warrants for the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, and his former defense minister Yoav Gallant, accusing them of war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza. The justice department has threatened California over alleged noncitizen voters.

In a letter addressed to the California secretary of state, Shirley Weber, on Tuesday, the acting deputy attorney general, Trent McCotter, said the justice department gave Los Angeles county officials a “password-protected thumb drive” with names of people that the federal government “believes are likely noncitizens”, Reuters first reported.

The letter, which gives state officials 48 hours to review the list, demands California withhold mail-in ballots from the listed people until their citizenship is confirmed, adding that ballots mailed back should be “segregated” and that those already returned should not be counted “until citizenship has been determined”.
The justice department added that if California officials do not comply, it “will have no choice but to seek emergency relief”.
“Allowing noncitizens to vote cancels citizen votes,” McCotter wrote in the letter.
The justice department’s latest threat comes as the Trump administration seeks evidence to support unverified claims of voter fraud ahead of next month’s midterm elections.

Paxton announced he would investigate an alleged conspiracy between pediatricians, vaccine makers and insurance companies in January, and at least one Texas pediatrician now says she is under investigation. Paxton linked his efforts to a campaign against vaccines from Donald Trump and Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and directly referenced the Maha movement in his announcement. The president endorsed Paxton’s Senate run in May.

Pointing to a sweeping collusion that “illegally incentivized” doctors to administer vaccines, Paxton alleges that the pharmaceutical and insurance industries were attempting to “bribe” medical providers.

He also launched an investigation into the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), accusing them in August of potentially recommending vaccines for financial gain – referencing a lawsuit the AAP filed earlier this year to halt sweeping changes to the childhood immunization schedule and once again invoking Trump and Kennedy’s moves on vaccines.

articles.headline: Microsoft and Japan took down a cybercrime network behind over a billion scam messages
keyFacts: Microsoft and Japan's National Police Agency dismantled a cybercrime network called YAM Store and two phishing kits.
The network enabled over one billion malicious messages targeting organizations worldwide and generated tens of millions of dollars.
Microsoft disabled over 20,000 accounts and blocked over 100,000 web domains connected to the scam marketplace.
body: We’ve all gotten a scam text about a nonexistent parking ticket or a fake package delivery, but hopefully you’ll start seeing fewer of them. Microsoft says it helped dismantle a marketplace for scammers sending phishing messages like those around the world. Through an investigation with Japan’s National Police Agency, it tracked scam activity back to a marketplace called YAM Store and a pair of phishing kits, CoGUI and Iron Man:
Microsoft and Japan took down a cybercrime network behind over a billion scam messages
Microsoft says it disabled over 20,000 accounts connected to a marketplace for scammers.

Since January 2026, YAM Store, CoGUI and Iron Man have collectively enabled more than one billion malicious messages targeting over 75,000 organizations worldwide, including more than 750 million messages geared toward Microsoft customers alone. These messages have been used to target consumers, healthcare organizations, financial institutions, and other businesses in more than 150 countries, generating tens of millions of dollars for their operators.

According to Microsoft’s report, scammers could buy stolen or fraudulent Microsoft and Google accounts on YAM Store and use the phishing kits to send scam messages. Microsoft says YAM Store also hijacked real organizations’ expired web domains and created websites for nonexistent organizations, which it used to get Microsoft accounts it could resell.

The Iron Man platform was also offering over 2,300 templates scammers could use to impersonate organizations like banks and police departments. Microsoft says it disabled over 20,000 accounts connected to YAM Store and blocked over 100,000 web domains being used for impersonation and fraud. With health sector cybersecurity non-profit Health-ISAC, Microsoft also seized and redirected web domains that were powering all three platforms.

articles.headline: Broncos dealt uncomfortable question from ESPN analyst on Bo Nix
keyFacts: ESPN analyst Dan Graziano speculated that the Denver Broncos could potentially bench struggling quarterback Bo Nix this season.
Nix has recorded 942 passing yards, six touchdowns, three interceptions, and a 41.5 QBR over the first five weeks of the season.
The Broncos are currently 3-2 and remain in contention, but offensive struggles have raised questions about whether a quarterback change could occur.
body: The Denver Broncos are currently 3-2 on the season, but there are some massive questions about this team, and specifically on the offensive side of the ball.

Sean Payton already took over play-calling, which didn't help in Week 5. Now, with one card pulled for how to improve the offense, the attention naturally shifts towards quarterback Bo Nix, who's struggling to begin the season.

There's enough worry with Nix right now that ESPN's Dan Graziano is speculating that the Broncos could make a QB change at some point this season. That's how bad things are going: an ESPN analyst believes Nix being benched isn't totally impossible.
ESPN insider speculates Broncos could bench Bo Nix

"And this is only speculative, but I wonder how long the Broncos will go with Bo Nix if he doesn't start playing better," Graziano writes. "They made the playcaller change for Week 5, and it didn't seem to work, so you start to wonder if the problem is the plays or the player."
Denver is 3-2, and they're in the hunt for the AFC West and an AFC Wild Card spot. However, enough questions are mounting about Nix's play that a change isn't totally inconceivable.
So far this season, Nix has 942 passing yards (21st in the NFL) with six passing touchdowns, three interceptions, and a 41.5 QBR (24th).
He's not been horrible, but Nix is clearly playing like a bottom-half-of-the-NFL QB through five weeks so far. For a Super Bowl contender, that's not good enough.
Denver needs Nix to start playing better. But if he continues to struggle and the Broncos are looking at a losing record at some point later in the year, a change is not totally out of the question.

Graziano is speculating, but it's noteworthy nonetheless. Behind Nix in the QB room are Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger. But if they decide to bench Nix, maybe they trade for Jacoby Brissett or some other veteran QB who can be a game manager for the Broncos.

With their elite defense, the Broncos shouldn't need a superstar QB to win it all this year. But someone who can make the right throws, protect the football, and raise the floor of this offense would make sense to add.

As much as that should be Nix this season, his struggles have opened the door for Denver to make a change. It's incredibly unlikely, but it's not something fans should totally write off from happening just yet.

body: If you’re not one of the roughly 230 million people who already own a copy of Grand Theft Auto V and you happen to have a PlayStation Plus Extra or Premium subscription, now is your last chance to get it play it on the service. As shared by users on Reddit, Sony has been blasting messages to PS5 owners letting them know that Once Upon A Time In Los Santos will be leaving the service on November 17, a mere two days ahead of GTA VI‘s November 19 release.

Cheekily, in addition to alerting people to the impending departure of GTA V, the warningÂ includes an option to pre-order GTA VI because with how huge the game is and how long it’s taken Rockstar to develop it, it needs every little boost it can get on the quest for profitability.

Players have a little more than a month to finish the game that’s been keeping the Grand Theft Auto candles burning for Rockstar (alongside GTA Online) for the last 13 years. The game has gone through three console generations and is, by Wikipedia’s accounting, the second best-selling game of all time, making it worth checking out if you’re not one of the millions who’ve already done so.

articles.headline: Manchester City v Paris Saint-Germain: Champions League – live
keyFacts: Paris Saint-Germain took a three-goal lead against Manchester City in the Champions League match with goals from Doué, Dembélé, and Vitinha.
Manchester City scored their first goal of the match in the 53rd minute when Erling Haaland powered in a header.
The match marked the first time Manchester City conceded three first-half goals at home in the Champions League.
body: GOAL! Manchester City 1-3 Paris Saint-Germain (Haaland 53)

Mendes really should be booked for wrapping his arms around Semenyo’s waist. But somehow no. Then from the free kick, Ndiaye nearly forces a low shot into the bottom left, only for Safonov to parry. But then he picks up possession again, swinging in from the left. Haaland power-glances a header across Safonov and into the top right! Is it on?
51 min: A PSG free kick near the centre circle. Nuno Mendes goes for goal, having spotted Donnarumma off his line. Not quite, but full marks for sass and ambition.

49 min: Semenyo dribbles artfully down the right and curls a cross towards Fernandez at the far stick. Fernandez has to convert this sensational cross … but slaps a downward header wide left. City should be on the scoresheet, and speaking of which, here’s Matt Dony with a quip he describes himself as the “lowest of low-hanging fruit … if City carry on playing this badly, it could end 1-114!”

48 min: Haaland barrels down the left and clips a low pass across to Semenyo, whose drive from the edge of the box is deflected high and wide. Haaland couldn’t get the ball out from under his feet to shoot himself. Anyway, the resulting corner comes to nothing, but City have flown out of the blocks here, clearly having been given the half-time what-for.
46 min: Two of the subs quickly into the action. Bouaddi creams a diagonal towards Ndiaye on the left. Ndiaye cuts into the box before hoicking harmlessly over.

Half-time postbag. “That 30-odd minutes of football from PSG is some of the best I’ve ever seen. At this level football transcends sport into something approaching art. Just amazing to watch” – Martin Gamage

“Say what you will about the tenets of the Qatari government, but at least they built a team worth the money. From spending a decade as Europe’s most dependable clown show, they’re now quite possibly the best club side since peak-Messi’s peak-Barcelona” – Walter Sobchak Kári Tulinius

“I thought I would enjoy City getting hammered, but it’s hard to muster anything above indifference. It’s all so artificial right now, like trying to get outraged over Cellophane. Bring on the charges/irrefutable evidence so we can all just move on. (I’m watching BSC Preussen v Altglienicke in the German fourth tier this weekend, now that’s proper football)” – Tim Woods
“With everything that is going on, if City score tonight will it be annotated as Asterix the Goal against the Parisians?” – Andy Gordon

“I’ve been pondering on a metaphor for City’s matches and I think they are like entries in The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy. Entertaining, beautifully crafted and attracting fervent fans, but only plausibly real, not actually real at all. Pep’s team were sometimes described as playing football from another planet - maybe they are now” – Gary Naylor
“People derided Arteta’s approach during the final but you simply can’t go toe to toe with this PSG team” – Arthur Simiyu
“Good plan, City have decided to be abysmal to take the pressure off and give the media a break!” – Chris, Corfu
“City need to spend seriously big money in January” – Andrew Goudie
“I sincerely hope that Enzo Maresca is only getting paid once for this sham…bolic performance tonight!” – Justin Kavanagh
45 min: This is the first time City have conceded three first-half goals at home in the Champions League. They’ll be delighted only two minutes of stoppage time are to be played.
44 min: … Guehi tries to hack clear, but only manages to slice back towards his own goal. Fortunately for him, straight at Donnarumma. City’s defenders have been all over the place.

41 min. … but this is better too. City win another corner, this time down the left, and from that, Guehi and Gvardiol get in each other’s way as they attempt to head goalwards from close range. The ball squirts harmlessly wide left.

40 min: Semenyo jinks down the right and enters the box along the touchline. His low cross-cum-shot is turned around the post by Pacho, but more through luck than design. The resulting corner leads to a rare period of City pressure, but Haaland can’t get a shot away when the ball nears him. PSG finally clear their lines. Better from City, though their bar is set so low this evening it may as well be subterranean.

38 min: Zaïre-Emery dribbles towards the City box with great elegance. He sits Khusanov down, but then can’t decide whether to look for Dembele or shoot himself. He does neither. But PSG launch another attack, and Hakimi shoots yet again. Straight at the keeper.

34 min: Fernandez bursts into the PSG box from the right, then goes over. He wants a penalty, but he’s hardly been brushed by Ruiz. Meanwhile, adding insult to injury, the PSG fans are now performing the Poznan.
33 min: The City players hold a quick meeting. They need to sort this out and quick. Pep with the thousand-yard stare in the stand; on the touchline, Marseca’s gaze clocks at least 1,001.
GOAL! Manchester City 0-3 Paris Saint-Germain (Vitinha 32)

A cross into the City box from the left. Hakimi’s header caroms off the left-hand post. But PSG don’t feel sorry for themselves. They come again., Zaire-Emery back-flicking Akliouche’s low right-wing cross back into the path of Vitinha, who opens his body and slams forensically into the right-hand side of the net. Donnarumma with no chance!

30 min: Zaïre-Emery’s drive is blocked by Guehi. Akliouche then brushes Semenyo off the ball. The referee’s whistle goes, awarding City a very generous foul. Akliouche, livid, lashes the ball into the net from long range. It won’t count, obviously, but neither is he booked.
29 min: Vitinha is given a little bit too much time to the left of the City D. He doesn’t catch his shot properly, and it’s claimed by Donnarumma before it can squeak into the bottom left.
27 min: PSG again with the metronomic passing, their fans again with the olés. The City of Manchester Stadium is otherwise pretty quiet, save for some pensive mumbling.

25 min: … but City come again, through Doku down the left. Doku wedges a cross into the middle for Haaland, who from close range should do much better with his header than send it sailing back through the six-yard box. The ball clanks out for a corner, from which nothing comes.
24 min: Semenyo crosses poorly from the right, looking for Haaland. As the ball sails high over the bar, the PSG fans – en fête – cheer in the hearty style.

23 min: Nuno Mendes should release Fabian Ruiz into acres down the right. But he clanks a seemingly simple pass straight at Guehi. Had he made it, Ruiz was one-on-one with Donnarumma and City were facing a world of pain.

19 min: Haaland takes matters into his own hands with a power-bustle down the middle. He reaches the box, but he’s been pushed a little to the left by Pacho, who then blocks the shot with a well-timed lunge … and nothing comes from the resulting corner. City and their fans a little bit stunned here.

17 min: One minute and 39 seconds elapsed between the goals. And it could be three, because Vitinha has a shot aimed for the bottom left deflected off Khusanov’s ankle and towards the bottom right, making things much easier for Donnarumma. On the touchline, all the blood drains from Enzo Maresca’s face.
GOAL! Manchester City 0-2 Paris Saint-Germain (Dembélé 15)

It’s a double whammy! In their very next attack, Dembélé crosses long from the right. Doué takes the ball down on the left, afforded too much space by Khusanov, and returns it to the far post, where Dembélé plants a header home!
GOAL! Manchester City 0-1 Paris Saint-Germain (Doue 13)

From the restart, PSG play their way upfield. From the right wing to the left. Doué cuts in from the flank and from the edge of the box, decides to see if he can trick Donnarumma at his near post. And he can do it! Having given the keeper the eyes, he whistles a low drive into the bottom left! That’s a hell of a move with a finish to match.

12 min: It wasn’t a penalty, but City do get a free kick, because at the end of the phase of play, Semenyo was fouled out on the left. Fernandez sends the set piece low towards the near post, where Safanov clumsily bundles the ball around his post. From the corner, Safonov punches the ball onto his own crossbar, then Semenyo skies a shot over the bar from six yards! But Guehi is penalised anyway for a shove on the keeper.

10 min: Cherki bursts into the PSG box down the left. Marquinhos sticks a leg across him. Cherki goes over. There’s contact – and a VAR check – but turns out Marquinhos got a touch on the ball. No penalty.

8 min: Akliouche looks to have won a corner off Gvardiol down the right, but the linesman awards a goal kick. From the restart, Semenyo gets a bit careless and allows Zaïre-Emery a shot. Donnarumma has it covered.
6 min: Semenyo surges down the inside-right channel but his flick towards Cherki on the wing is no good. But that’s City’s first sortie into enemy territory.
2 min: Cherki is caught dozing by Dembélé, who sends Doué scampering down a cul-de-sac on the left. Cherki will be pleased Khusanov was on point there.

The teams make it onto the pitch … after a fashion. City left their visitors waiting in the tunnel for a couple of minutes. Then the Champions League theme, to the usual chorus of disgust. As loud as the Uefa-focused opprobrium usually is? Not sure; it’s almost as though City fans have their minds on a different admin-infused opponent. Whatever, the atmosphere seems a little subdued; everyone’s been through the ringer, one way or the other, in recent weeks. Sure it’ll get going in a minute when the match eventually kicks off (late).
Pep Guardiola is indeed in the house. He’s sat behind City director of football Hugo Viana in the executive box. A mosaic in the stand: CTID. City Til I Die.

Enzo Maresca speaks to TNT. “It’s a special night … Champions League night against the best team in Europe … hopefully we can win the game … I know Pep [Guardiola] will be here but he was not at the training ground [earlier today] and I did not speak with him … by showing support to the club even when he is not here, for sure it’s a special moment for him tonight also … he is back to his home … also for the fans, they will be happy to see Pep here tonight … to beat PSG you need a complete performance … on and off the ball … we are going to create some chances and concede some chances … we need to find the right balance.”

Manchester City go strong in the wake of their 3-0 win at Anfield. Jeremy Doku, Abdukodir Khusanov and Josko Gvardiol replace Iliman Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly in the starting XI. PSG haven’t quite gone so strong, in so much as Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is only on the bench. But then again he can come off it later when everyone else is a bit knackered, so it’s swings and roundabouts. Ferran Torres, erstwhile of City, is also named as a sub.
Shall we set the scene? Let me cede the floor to Matt Hughes …

… and so the recent history of the winners of three of the last four editions of the Champions League is told. Opinions regarding the state of it (no pun intended) may vary. Kick-off is at 8pm BST. It’s on!

articles.headline: Federal court bars California law requiring ICE officers to wear visible identification
keyFacts: The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals blocked California from enforcing a law requiring federal immigration officers to wear visible identification.
The panel ruled that the state cannot dictate how federal agents carry out their work under the Supremacy Clause.
The preliminary injunction prevents enforcement of the identification requirement while the ongoing lawsuit continues.
body: The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals barred California on Wednesday from enforcing a law requiring federal immigration officers to identify themselves while on duty, ruling that the state cannot dictate how federal agents carry out their work.

The three-judge panel granted the federal government a preliminary injunction against the identification provision of California’s No Vigilantes Act. The decision reverses a lower-court ruling that had refused to block the law.

“As before, we conclude that the United States is likely to succeed on the merits of its Supremacy Clause claim because … [the] No Vigilantes Act attempts to directly regulate the United States in its performance of governmental functions, and Congress has not authorized such regulation,” U.S. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, a nominee of President Donald Trump , wrote in the opinion . He was joined on the panel by U.S. Circuit Judge Jacqueline Nguyen, a nominee of former President Barack Obama, and U.S. Circuit Judge Daniel Collins, another Trump nominee.

“In sum, if a state law directly regulates the governmental conduct of the United States without congressional authorization, it is void irrespective of whether the regulated activities are essential to federal functions or operations, and irrespective of the degree to which the state law interferes with such functions or operations,” Bennett added.
The ruling does not end the lawsuit. Rather, it prevents California from enforcing the identification requirement against federal officers while the case continues.

Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-CA) signed the two laws in September 2025 as part of legislation responding to Trump’s immigration enforcement operations. Newsom criticized federal agents for arresting U.S. citizens, concealing their identities, and undermining transparency.

“For Trump and Miller, the only metric is mass arrests, detentions and removals — even at the expense of Americans’ constitutional rights,” Newsom said at the time, referring to White House deputy chief of staff for policy Stephen Miller.

The Justice Department sued California, Newsom, and state Attorney General Rob Bonta on Nov. 17, 2025, challenging provisions of both laws before it was set to go into effect in January 2026. The federal government argued that the measures improperly regulated federal law enforcement operations and that the mask restrictions discriminated against the federal government.

The district court declined to block the identification requirement, finding that the government had not shown the law would interfere with federal immigration enforcement, prompting the federal government to appeal.

“Security concerns exist for federal law enforcement officers with or without masks,” U.S. District Judge Christina Snyder, a nominee of former President Bill Clinton, wrote in February. “If anything, the court finds that the presence of masked and unidentifiable individuals, including law enforcement, is more likely to heighten the sense of insecurity for all.”
ILHAN OMAR IMMIGRATION HISTORY: SCRUTINY SURROUNDS FAMILY’S REFUGEE CLAIMS

Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward Jr. welcomed the decision, posting on social media that California cannot dictate how federal law enforcement officers perform duties authorized by Congress.
“Today’s decision is a huge WIN for protecting the safety of our Nation’s law enforcement officers and ensuring @POTUS’s promise to enforce our Nation’s immigration laws,” Woodward said.

articles.headline: Rep. Ilhan Omar investigated in DC, Minnesota over inflating net worth, immigration fraud: sources
keyFacts: Rep. Ilhan Omar is the subject of federal investigations regarding potential immigration fraud and the inflation of her net worth on House disclosure forms, according to sources and officials.
Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a search warrant at Omar's Washington, D.C., residence, and grand jury subpoenas were issued to family members, including her sister.
Omar's office stated that the financial disclosure errors resulted from an accounting discrepancy and dismissed the investigations as a politically motivated smear campaign.
body: WASHINGTON — Rep. Ilhan Omar is the target of at least two federal investigations related to possible immigration fraud and inflation of her net worth by tens of millions of dollars in House disclosure forms, according to sources familiar with the probes and an administration official.

DC US Attorney Jeanine Pirro confirmed Tuesday on Fox News’ “America Reports” that “there are several investigations going on” related to the Minnesota Democrat, adding that potential civil or criminal immigration violations as well as Omar’s claim of being worth up to $30 million were also under scrutiny.

Sources familiar with the cases disclosed that the Minnesota US Attorney’s Office was leading the probe into alleged immigration fraud, possibly involving false statements about Omar’s birth date, while Pirro’s office in DC was taking on the inquiry into the finances of Omar and her husband, Tim Mynett.

Concealing material facts or willfully misrepresenting information on immigration papers could lead to the congresswoman’s denaturalization, one source said. It’s unclear whether those alleged crimes occurred on paperwork originally compiled by her father or on subsequent forms such as a passport renewal.

Federal investigators are also looking at whether Omar’s father, Nur Omar Mohamed, lied about his service in the Somalian military under the Marxist dictator Mohamed Siad Barre, The Washington Post reported.

The Omar family emigrated first to Kenya during the bloody civil war that led to Barre’s toppling. They eventually arrived in the US in 1995. Omar’s father died of complications due to COVID-19 in 2020.
Criminal denaturalizations have a 10-year statute of limitations, while civil denaturalizations aren’t subject to such limitations.

“A conviction for knowingly procuring naturalization unlawfully requires revocation of citizenship,” said Todd Spodek, a federal criminal defense lawyer. “But the Supreme Court has made clear that not every false statement is enough; the government generally must show the lie actually mattered to obtaining citizenship.

“The Constitution requires seven years of citizenship to serve in the House. Denaturalization can operate retroactively, but how that would affect an already-seated member of Congress is largely untested,” Spodek added. “A criminal conviction alone does not automatically remove a member from office.”
Omar has already been investigated twice by a House watchdog, the Office of Congressional Conduct, for omitting information from financial forms, but the allegations were dismissed both times.
In 2024, she astoundingly claimed that her and Mynett’s joint assets were valued between $5 million and $30 million, only to file disclosures one year later, claiming between $20,000 and $125,000.
The previously high-valued assets were largely attributable to income reported from Mynett’s wine and venture capital businesses, which recorded a meager $200 to $1,000 last year.
Omar’s office said the error was a result of an accounting “discrepancy.”

The 44-year-old lawmaker has said she became a US citizen as a minor in 2000 as a result of her father receiving the same benefit — meaning she would have had to have been under 18 years old at the time.
Some publicly accessible records, however, list Omar’s birthdate as Oct. 4, 1981, rather than the same date in 1982, meaning she would no longer have been a minor when her dad became a citizen.

In response to other accusations about immigration fraud allegedly involving one of her brothers, Omar’s campaign told the Associated Press in 2018 that she didn’t have a birth certificate due to her family’s displacement by the long-running Somalia civil war.

Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents executed a search warrant Monday on Omar’s DC bungalow and exited the home carrying boxes of apparent evidence that will be used for the immigration-related probe.
“They got a warrant signed by a federal judge,” Pirro said in defending the raid on the “Squad” Democrat’s residence.

“There’s no question that that judge would not have signed that warrant unless there was probable cause. And probably more than that, given the individual who was involved and given the fact that we’re in the nation’s capital — with judges in the nation’s capital,” she added.
A Department of Justice spokesperson confirmed Monday’s raid was part of a federal criminal investigation, which one source with knowledge of the probe said had been ongoing for years.
Grand jury subpoenas have also been issued to family members of the Minnesota congresswoman, including to one of her sisters, Sahra Noor, the New York Times first reported Tuesday.
Omar lashed out at President Trump after the HSI search, claiming she “will not be silenced.”
“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation,” she said.
“The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong,” added a rep for her office.
Trump said Monday that he had “nothing to do” with the probe of Omar but called her a “totally crooked” politician.
“I think she’s a terrible person. Just a complainer. She comes from a country that is a non-country. And then she comes over here, and she complains about our Constitution,” the president said.
Later Tuesday, Trump posted on his Truth Social about Omar’s revision of her net worth in House financial disclosures from $30 million down to just around the low six figures.
Neither Noor nor reps for Omar’s office immediately responded to requests for comment Wednesday.

body: The American League Championship Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians shifts to Cleveland for Games 3-5 after the teams won one game apiece in Tampa Bay. Game 3 is set for Thursday and was originally scheduled to start at 6 p.m. ET, but MLB has announced that the game has been moved up to 1 p.m. ET due to "forecasted inclement weather" in the Cleveland area.
"The change, which is based on forecasted rain on Thursday night in Cleveland, is being made proactively in order to remain on schedule in the ALCS," MLB said.

A few hours later, Major League Baseball also decided to move up NLCS Game 4 between the Milwaukee Brewers and Los Angeles Dodgers. That game is being played in L.A.'s Dodger Stadium and was set for 9 p.m. ET. That's 8 p.m. in Milwaukee and 6 p.m. in Los Angeles, but it appears the league wanted that 8 p.m. ET time slot now without real fears of overlap from the ALCS.

The Cleveland area forecast as of Wednesday midday shows rain and scattered thunderstorms late at night and overnight. In glancing at hourly forecasts, it's possible a 6 p.m. ET start would allow the game to finish before any weather issues, but the league is being proactive to ensure the final few innings aren't affected by weather. It's a good move. No one ever wants to see the late innings interrupted and suspending a game until the next day is a major problem.

Looking ahead at the forecast, with Game 4 scheduled for Friday and Game 5 for Saturday, there could be further problems. On Friday, current forecasts around Cleveland call for rain throughout the day, though in the evening it is expected to be "light." At present, the game on Friday is scheduled for 6 p.m. ET. If there is an NLCS Game 5, it would be at 9 p.m. ET. Should the Brewers sweep the Dodgers, perhaps the league would move the ALCS game back.
The Guardians took Game 1 of the ALCS in Tampa Bay before dropping Game 2 on Tuesday night. Gavin Williams will be on the mound for Cleveland and opposed by the Rays' Griffin Jax.

articles.headline: FIFA seeking rule change to avoid repeat of Folarin Balogun World Cup scandal
keyFacts: FIFA is set to amend its rules to prevent automatic one-match suspensions, aiming to avoid a repeat of the Folarin Balogun World Cup scandal.
Balogun avoided a suspension after his red card following an intervention, sparking heavy criticism from sporting bodies like UEFA.
The proposal will be discussed at the FIFA Council meeting on Thursday amid ongoing pressure on FIFA president Gianni Infantino.
body: FIFA are poised to amend its rules to prevent suspensions from automatic one-match bans.
The tweak is being made to avoid a repeat of the Folarin Balogun scandal that rocked the World Cup.
Balogun scored three goals at the World Cup Getty
What happened with Folarin Balogun at the World Cup?
Balogun was sent off during the United States’ round of 32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina, which triggered an automatic one-game suspension.
However, the decision was overturned following an intervention from the White House and the forward was permitted to play in the USMNT’S last-16 tie against Belgium, which they lost.
The motion is set to be discussed at the first session of the 37-member FIFA Council on Thursday.
talkSPORT understands the proposal is viewed as FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who claims he played no role in the decision, addressing the Balogun scandal.
It is also understood the wording was rushed through on Tuesday evening and Infantino’s critics still want all correspondence shared from the incident.
Balogun’s reprieve sparked significant reaction from several sporting bodies, including UEFA, of which Belgium is a member.

“Yesterday’s decision to suspend for a probationary period of a year the implementation of the one-match automatic suspension following the red card issued to the player Folarin Balogun crossed a read line,” a UEFA statement read.
“Football, like any other sports, relies on rules, which are the basis for fair, honest and transparent competition.
“Sometimes rules are open to interpretation. In this case not.
“A minimum automatic suspension of one match following a red card is not a discretionary option and does not require the decision of a competent body to be enacted.
Infantino’s decisions throughout the summer have put him under serious pressure to keep his job Getty

“It is a principle embedded in regulations, which cannot be made subject to exceptions, let alone in the middle of a tournament where several other players have been in the same situation and regularly served their suspension.”
UEFA additionally labelled it an ‘unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable decision.’
Gianni Infantino’s nightmare summer
Thursday’s meeting marks the first time the council has gathered following Infantino’s controversial plan to sell the World Cup was revealed.
The scheme was met with widespread condemnation, as the FA, UEFA and CONCACAF all released strongly-worded statements in response.
Infantino’s controversial summer has now left him facing a serious battle to be re-elected as FIFA president.
Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega is the only other confirmed candidate, while Arsene Wenger was endorsed by former Arsenal pupil Emmanuel Petit for the role.
The deadline for candidates to be nominated is November 18, with elections to take place at the 77th FIFA Congress in March.

articles.headline: Epic Is Overhauling Its Anti-Cheat So That Fortnite Can Finally Come To A New Platform
keyFacts: Epic Games announced it is working on a Linux version of Fortnite to test an overhaul of its Easy Anti-Cheat software.
Epic said it will pilot the new Easy Anti-Cheat Linux version in Fortnite first before eventually making it available to other game developers.
Epic has not shared a release timeline for Fortnite on Linux, though the pilot program will be available through a new preview launcher.
body: Thanks to devices such as the Steam Deck and Steam Machine, as well as the ongoing issues with Windows, gaming on Linux looks a lot more attractive over the last few years. Its biggest hurdle is still multiplayer games and their anti-cheat systems, but Epic Games is committed to bringing one of the biggest around to the operating system soon.

Epic Games has announced that it is working on a Linux version for Fortnite. It's going to act as a test for Epic's overhaul of EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat) , its solution to those developing multiplayer games in Unreal Engine to prevent cheating (most recently used in Gears of War: E-Day). Epic says that it has offered Linux support for its current version of EAC, but that most developers (itself included) opted not to use it and instead omit Linux support entirely because of its inability to be as protective as its Windows version.

A native rebuild of EAC, that doesn't require translation layers such as Proton, would help Epic bring the software up to par with Windows, at which point it would be comfortable finally releasing a native Linux version of Fortnite. In a blog post, Epic says that once it has reached this stage, it will make this available to other developers, too.

"We are also planning to pilot EAC Linux v2 in Fortnite first, where we’ll test it in a live environment and refine it based on what we learn. Once we’ve validated EAC v2’s effectiveness, we’ll make it available to more game developers so they can bring their multiplayer games to Linux players too."

Epic hasn't shared a timeline for when it expects Fortnite on Linux, but does say that its pilot program will be available through its new Epic Game Store launcher . Announced at the same time, Epic has decided to follow through with its commitment to AI-developed software earlier this week, with the new launcher labelled as "vibe coded" because "programming is hard". This version is still in preview and lacks all of the features currently on the main version of the store launcher, but Epic says that it is already seeing some speed improvements (even if they're just a few seconds here or there).

That might be too steep a price to pay depending on your appetite for linking your credit card details to an app that is being iterated on without much (or any) human intervention. And it's already led to some strange bugs that certainly would've been caught without being rushed into the hands of users.

articles.headline: Aboard an icebreaker, a writer got a closer look at the Arctic's 'Sea Change'
keyFacts: Aboard an icebreaker, a writer got a closer look at the Arctic's 'Sea Change' As polar ice melts in the Arctic, shipping lanes are opening up, making the region a new zone of superpower competition.
Writer Rana Foroohar got an up-close look aboard the USS Healy, a Coast Guard icebreaker.
She says that traversing the North Pole by ship — once a "largely conceptual" route — is now becoming a "real possibility" for two or three weeks a year.
body: Aboard an icebreaker, a writer got a closer look at the Arctic's 'Sea Change'

As polar ice melts in the Arctic, shipping lanes are opening up, making the region a new zone of superpower competition. Writer Rana Foroohar got an up-close look aboard the USS Healy, a Coast Guard icebreaker. She says that traversing the North Pole by ship — once a "largely conceptual" route — is now becoming a "real possibility" for two or three weeks a year.

"If you are taking one of these Arctic routes, you can save as much as 40% of the time it would take you to go from the Atlantic to the Pacific, and depending on the price of oil, that's a heck of a lot of money," she says. "China and Russia together are clearly trying to make the top of the world an area over which they have the most interest."

In her new book, Sea Change: America's New Great Game in the Arctic Circle, Foroohar makes the case that the "High North" may become as critical to world shipping as the Suez or Panama canals. But she also notes that beneath the Arctic waters are large deposits of oil, natural gas and rare earth minerals, as well as underwater cables, which carry a large part of the world's intercontinental information flow.

"Undersea cables have become a real touchstone in wars and conflicts around the world," she says. "So you are seeing a race to lay down new cable, and who can get there fastest, and then who can potentially commercialize and even militarize areas where those cables have been laid."

Foroohar describes the Arctic Circle as one of the few areas of the globe where countries and companies can still "hunt" for territory and "duke it out potentially with rivals." And she predicts more conflict in the coming decades as the region continues to warm.

"There is going to be more commerce done through this area. There is gonna be greater military interest in the area, and all of that matters because it really is in America's backyard," she says. "I just think that everything in the High North is going to be higher priority for America in the future."
Interview highlights
On increased international interest in the Arctic

China and Russia together are clearly trying to make the top of the world an area over which they have the most interest. And that's very interesting because it starts to dovetail with something that's happening in U.S. policy, which is more of a sense of we need to protect what's close to home. And so if you look at things that way, then you have the U.S. and China coming into much closer geographic conflict. Whether or not it would ever be a hot conflict, I hope not, but certainly competition in that area.
On the debate over rights to resources in international waters

There's some debate over that. There is something called the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, which governs maritime activities, including those in the Arctic. It has ... rules about where you can mine, how you can mine, who gets what. But the U.S. never signed on to that convention. Various presidents from Clinton to Bush [to] Obama did support it, but key Republican senators opposed it, basically on ideological grounds, the notion that no international body should have sovereign right over what the U.S. does. ... And so it makes it much more of a free-for-all as to who gets what in the Arctic. And then you throw in the fact that Russians and Chinese don't always play by the U.N. rules either.
On how Arctic power struggles are part of a larger global trend

It's kind of part and parcel of a bigger collapse of international rule and a pendulum shift from globalization to something that is much more about regionalization and spheres of power ... and influence, which is exactly what's happening in the Arctic, which to me is so interesting, not only just for itself, but because it's a mirror into what's happening in other parts of the world. Some of the same conflicts over territory and mineral rights and ports that you see in the Arctic now are also happening in Latin America or West Africa or parts of the South China Sea. So it's a bit of a bellwether for geostrategy more broadly. …

And then there's this — kind of largely theoretical up until now, but becoming more realistic — trans-polar route where right now it might be a couple of weeks that you could consider going right across the pole, but if global warming continues the way it seems to be going in the next decade or two, that could turn into a month, two months, three months. And so who's going to control that area? This is what's up for stake now.
On what it's like to be onboard an Arctic icebreaker

You begin to feel and hear the ice as it is being broken by the ship. And I remember being down on the mess hall, which is a couple floors down from the waterline, and I was sitting eating my lunch and you begin to hear this shhhhhh kind of sound, like something traveling through sound, and then it becomes squeaky, like fingers on chalkboard, and you can kind of feel vibration and it gets louder and louder and you're like, "Wow, there are only 12 inches of reinforced steel between me and death." That's very sobering.
On the region's changing climate

I actually touched base with some of those scientists several months after we had come off of the Healy, and they were starting to go through that data and look at it. And there is some real scientific data showing that these areas are changing. They are warming. They are becoming different than they have been in the past. And that affects all kinds of things. It affects the kind of fish that could live there. It affects wind and wave patterns that you might get, which could in turn affect things like the Canadian boreal forest fires that I experience in my home in Brooklyn, New York. You would think that has nothing to do with the Arctic, but it actually has everything to do with what's happening in the High North.
Therese Madden and Susan Nyakundi produced and edited this interview for broadcast. Bridget Bentz, Molly Seavy-Nesper and Beth Novey adapted it for the web.

articles.headline: Trump-backed GOP candidate who ousted scandal-plagued incumbent warns against 'never-ending war' with Iran
keyFacts: Ryan Elijah defeated incumbent Cory Mills in the August 18 Republican primary with 47% of the vote.
Elijah warned against a never-ending war with Iran while emphasizing the need to prevent a nuclear Iran.
Elijah will face Navy veteran Bale Dalton in the November 3 general election.
body: For 14 years, Ryan Elijah reported on Central Florida’s biggest stories from the television newsroom. Now, he is on a mission to represent the same community in Congress.

Elijah stepped into a contentious GOP primary in which he warned that incumbent Cory Mills was at risk of losing the Republican-leaning district to the Democrats, following a series of personal and professional scandals.
Elijah won a convincing victory in the August 18 Republican primary, receiving 47% of the vote to Mills' 34%.
Trump, who had originally endorsed Mills, later claimed that he had privately encouraged the embattled congressman to withdraw from the race.
REP CORY MILLS DRAWS FIRST REPUBLICAN CHALLENGER AS SEXUAL MISCONDUCT ALLEGATIONS, EXPULSION THREAT MOUNT

Recently, the veteran television journalist sat down with Fox News Digital to discuss his views on Iran, affordability, and immigration, while pledging to remain an independent voice in Congress, and a strong advocate for Volusia and Seminole counties .
Elijah did not take the decision to leave working in media lightly, but felt a call to leadership:

"I love my job. It's something I could have retired from TV and been perfectly happy. But I think we all look for the time you're asked to step up and lead. And for me, that was this time. When we saw how the primary was playing out, it just became clear that we were going to lose this election in November.

"And I decided that we had the connections in this community to throw our hat in the ring. We had the trust from the community and the primary played out a lot like we thought it would, where people wanted a choice. I think that's what primaries are all about in Seminole County and Volusia County spoke really loud. In that primary, and now I think they put us in a great spot to hold this seat in November."
Elijah pledges to put transparency and accountability front and center for the constituents of the seventh district:

"Well, I think transparency and accountability are huge issues. I think when I talk to people, they don't feel like they're heard very much in Washington. And I think that you have to be transparent about whatever you can. And first of all, if you have nothing to hide, that's the best way to be transparent because you can exactly show your business dealings and how your life dealings are.

"And that's something we've talked about a lot…and then in terms of accountability, no one is above the law. And that's a message that Americans want to hear, whether you're a Democrat or Republican, there are laws for a reason, and we have to make sure those laws are upheld."
As the military engagement with Iran is rattling global energy markets and pinching Americans' pocketbooks, Elijah concedes the need to thwart a nuclear Iran, but also is wary of another forever war:
GOP RISING STAR HELPED TOPPLE TRUMP-BACKED INCUMBENT. NOW HE'S CAUGHT LEADERSHIP'S EYE

"This is a decade-long issue and a conflict between Iran and its proxies, where they have targeted and they have killed Americans . So the U.S. military right now is trying to end that conflict. But as representatives, we have to listen to the American people. We have to listen to central Floridians.

"And they have been very clear on this. They're concerned about it. They are concerned this is going to be a never-ending war. They don't want that. I don't want that either. I share that belief, which is why I think we need to draw this conflict down. And we need to make sure that Iran is not a nuclear threat."
On the immigration issue, Elijah cites improvement under GOP leadership on the issue, but argues that enforcement focus should remain on criminals:

"This is another issue where I think you have to look at where we've come from. When you let tens of millions of illegal people into this country, you're going to have issues that take a long time to fix. And I think if you look at the way there has to be a federal, a local, and a state cooperation with immigration, that's what it takes to work. Which is why when I talk to all the sheriffs in our district that are endorsing us, they're handling immigration much better than other parts around the country because they have that cooperation.

"We need to start with the criminals. We have got many criminals still here illegally in the United States. That's what they focused on in central Florida. That's what ICE needs to focus on , removing the criminals. And there's a compassionate way to handle this as we've got an issue that is not going to be fixed in just six or 12 months."
Elijah consistently emphasizes that he will be an independent voice for the district, not a partisan rubber stamp:
"Well, I've said a lot. Look, I ran in this primary without the president's endorsement. I've been an independent voice in this and I've told a lot of people that ask me that question.

"As you can imagine, I go to a lot of doors. That's a question: ‘Will you support the president? Will you not support the president?’ And what I tell them is, if it's a policy that supports our country and supports our district, I'm going to support that policy.
"More often than not, I will because I'm a Republican. I like a lot of those policies. If there's a policy I disagree with, we won't. So in that situation, that's where things are at."
Finally, Elijah acknowledges that affordability, while lacking a quick and easy fix, is the defining 2026 issue for much of the electorate:

"I think the number one thing that we hear from people, and that's affordability, and that's not an easy fix, but I think what they want out of government is accountability. We talked about that before, that government is going to be accountable on its spending, on its policies, and getting inflation down, which is going to lower interest rates. It's going to lower the cost of living.

"People in Central Florida, people around the country, they want to be heard. And what they're saying in a very clear tone right now is make sure that you control government spending and protect the future of our children. That's probably the biggest thing I want them to notice."
Elijah will be facing Navy veteran and former NASA employee Bale Dalton in the November 3 general election.

articles.headline: Your flu shot can’t wait
keyFacts: Federal data shows the flu season is starting earlier than usual, with infections rising in all 50 states as of October 7.
Experts say a virologist suggested a mutation might help variants evade immunity, while international travel could also play a role.
Officials recommend getting the flu shot as soon as possible, along with washing hands, masking when sick, and consulting a doctor.
body: Some parts of the country are seeing levels of flu activity typically associated with late fall or early winter. | ﻿Deb Cohn-Orbach/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images
This story appeared in Today, Explained, a daily newsletter that helps you understand the most compelling news and stories of the day. Subscribe here .

Flu season is starting earlier than usual this year, which I know from reviewing federal data. But I also know it because I woke up with body aches and chills last night, mere days before I’d planned to get my flu vaccination (!).

Already, some parts of the country are seeing levels of flu activity typically associated with late fall or early winter. In Washington state, for instance, doctors are reporting seeing as much flu now as they usually would around Christmas.

Flu activity overall is still low , to be clear. But as of October 7, infections were rising in all 50 states. And flu is spreading before many people — like, say, me — have received their annual vaccine.

Epidemiologists don’t yet know why the flu arrived early this year, or why cases first started rising in Western states like Washington, California, and Nevada. It’s possible that a mutation is helping this year’s flu variants evade existing immunity, one virologist told NPR . International travel could play a role , too: Flu cases also spiked early in Japan and other parts of Asia.
We don’t need to know why the flu arrived early to take some basic precautions, though. So today, we’re talking through some practical tips for coping with an early flu season.
Go a little deeper
View Link

An early flu season doesn’t necessarily mean a worse season — but even a moderate season can do serious damage. Last year, influenza sent hundreds of thousands of people to the hospital and caused tens of thousands of deaths, including almost 200 among children .

The first and best way to avoid those kinds of harms is by getting the flu shot, which reduces the risk of serious illness by an average of 40 to 60 percent. In the US, people aged 6 months and older are typically told to get the vaccine by October’s end.
In light of the early onset, however (it takes two weeks to build up full immunity), you might instead want to get your shot ASAP.

There are some everyday precautions you can take, too — many of them familiar from the Covid-19 era. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and warm water, for slightly longer than feels appropriate. Mask when you’re sick or might encounter someone else who is.

And don’t neglect the good habits that support your overall health: getting enough sleep, drinking a lot of water, and eating a balanced diet. (There’s very little evidence for trendier interventions, like supplements, saunas, cold plunges, or the infused herbal baths that my kooky former yoga teacher used to recommend.)

If you do get flu symptoms, reach out to your doctor early — especially if you’re older, pregnant, immunocompromised, or otherwise at higher risk for complications. Prescription antiviral medications, like Tamiflu, prevent the flu virus from spreading inside your body so that your immune system can clear it. But they work best within 48 hours of symptom onset.

To be clear, you needn’t take my word on any of this; I’m just another voice in the public health cacophony! Besides, recent polling suggests that my particular voice — that is, the voice of someone who works in media — is not quite as persuasive as it used to be. (Ditto medical websites and government health agencies.)

But if you have doubts or questions about vaccines, there is someone much closer to home you can consult : Ask your doctor (or nurse or pharmacist) about the flu shot’s risks and benefits. They’re best positioned to break the science down and apply it to your health. In hindsight, mine surely would have told me to stop delaying my shot for a more convenient weekend.

articles.headline: Water-resistant and easy to clean: HP delivers an AMD Ryzen keyboard PC that can be splashed with liquid — EliteBoard G1a has a 32Whr battery but alas no touchpad, review finds
keyFacts: ComputerBase reviewed HP's EliteBoard G1a keyboard PC and found it to be a well-executed device with a high price tag of 2,149 euros.
HP claims the built-in keyboard is spill-resistant and easy to clean, and testing showed the 32Wh battery lasted over six hours.
The review noted that the system lacks a touchpad, has limited local AI performance, and faces stiff competition from mini PCs and desktops.
body: - ComputerBase's full test finds HP's EliteBoard G1a a well-executed keyboard PC whose biggest problem is its €2,149 price tag
- HP promises a spill-resistant, easy-clean keyboard designed to pass MIL-STD-810, but you probably shouldn't submerge it in water
- The 32Wh battery ran an impressive 6h 21m against HP's 3.5-hour claim, though it powered no display in said test

HP's EliteBoard G1a, the Windows PC built into a full-size keyboard that the company first showcased at CES 2026, has now undergone a full lab test at German outlet ComputerBase, and the verdict is broadly favorable.
In its review, ComputerBase concludes that the keyboard PC is not just an interesting idea but a well-executed one.

Its biggest weakness is the very high price, shared with practically all PC hardware that launched this year that could define it as a reach versus a must-have for many consumers and IT departments alike.
Skipping a touchpad by design and a short memory leash in tow

The review unit pairs AMD's Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350, a Kraken Point chip with four Zen 5 and four Zen 5c cores, Radeon 860M graphics, and a 50 TOPS NPU, with a single 32GB DDR5-5600 SO-DIMM and a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD.

All of that sits beneath the keys of a chassis measuring 358 x 119 x 18mm and 670g. Connectivity includes two rear USB-C ports (one USB4 with DisplayPort 2.1b, one 10Gbps), Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, stereo speakers, and two microphones.
The keyboard passes MIL-STD-810 testing per HP, and testing found it overwhelmingly supports its product page claims of a "spill-resistant, easy-clean keyboard."

Its more practical safeguard might be servicability: HP says the top-mounted keyboard module can be replaced in under 10 minutes, and ComputerBase confirms the bottom panel opens quickly, giving access to the RAM, SSD, and Wi-Fi module.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!

The EliteBoard also skips a touchpad, but it was never meant to have one; HP ships every unit with a pre-paired HP 675M wireless mouse that seems to do the job in spades, and the reviewer had no complaints, though others have been less forgiving of its absence.

The reviewer's gripes, however, lay elsewhere: they considered two USB-C ports potentially too few and recommend budgeting for a USB-C hub with HDMI, Ethernet, and USB-A, which is how it connected to their own test monitor.
They also found that neither HP's update tools nor Windows Update would move the AMD graphics driver past an October 2025 release, though a manual Adrenalin install worked without issue.

The keyboard-cum-computer has respectable performance but has design limitations that hold it back: with only one SO-DIMM installed, the APU runs in single-channel mode, which AMD's chips tend to punish.

More importantly, after an initial turbo burst above 50W, AMD's Skin Temperature Aware Power Management (STAPM) caps the chip at about 75% of its package power target, roughly 25W, to keep the keyboard surface comfortable.
The result is a Cinebench 2024 multi-core score of 794, slightly behind the 841 ComputerBase recorded from the same chip in Sapphire's Edge AI mini PC.

Though it isn't the intended use case, gaming is largely off the table, with Cyberpunk 2077 averaging 14.1fps at 1080p on high settings, indicating that the EliteBoard G1a largely caters to professionals and enterprises and makes no pretenses otherwise, despite its decent iGPU.

HP's "Next Gen AI PC" branding might be another bone of contention because, while the unit is capable of running AI onboard, it is notoriously slow at this task; in LM Studio, Qwen3 14B ran at 3.9 tokens per second on the CPU and 4.2 on the GPU, while the NPU could not be used at all. Local AI does work on the EliteBoard, the review concedes, but only within tight limits and at a lethargic pace at best.

The 32Wh battery is fitted to all three German configurations but is optional, or absent, in other markets. HP claims 3.5 hours of runtime. ComputerBase measured six hours and 21 minutes in the Procyon office test and four hours and 18 minutes streaming 4K YouTube, suggesting HP's numbers may understate what the unit can do in most use cases.
This might not offset the cost, however: ComputerBase's test configuration carries an MSRP of €2,149, and the cheapest German model starts at €1,299 with four cores and half the RAM and storage.

In the US, ComputerBase found that HP's configurator charges an extra $1,900 to go from 16GB and 512GB to 32GB across two modules and up to 2TB of storage, pushing a configured system to $4,632, while the advertised 64GB option is not offered at all.

Given the price tag and the niche it caters to, one can conclude that the EliteBoard will likely have a hard time in its niche, squeezed between classic desktops and mini PCs on one side and genuinely mobile notebooks on the other, even as it offers precious little versus a Mini PC, many of which double as much more capable AI systems for a considerably high price tag and lack of upgrade potential in tow.

It is, however, an intriguing option that can move from one workplace to another without losing progress, but whether that justifies the premium at a time when consumers are increasingly concerned about higher component prices remains to be seen.

Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick and Florian Wirtz shone after recent criticism as Liverpool thrashed LASK 6-3 to earn their second win in the Champions League.

Barcola kick-started his Liverpool career, having not scored or assisted in six appearances since his £123m move from Paris Saint-Germain, while Wirtz responded to calls for him to be dropped with a fine performance in what was expected to be a comfortable evening against the Austrian Bundesliga champions.

Liverpool had 19 shots in the opening period, a new record for an away team in the first half of a Champions League game, as Ronald Araujo headed in his first goal for the club before Barcola got off the mark with a tidy finish and then slotted in another from a Wirtz pass.

Iraola benched Virgil van Dijk in Austria for only the third time in Liverpool's 39 Champions League games since 2022, but when he and Joe Gomez were introduced at centre-back in the 62nd minute, they conceded three times.

Barcola's hat-trick, a tap-in from Frimpong's cross, followed Robert Ljubicic's consolation before Wales striker Lewis Koumas, leading the line in Alexander Isak's absence, deservedly scored Liverpool's sixth after he had two efforts ruled out for offside.

Finding balance in this Liverpool side was a factor in Arne Slot's dismissal and something Andoni Iraola has struggled with early in his time at the club.

The attack hasn't been free-flowing this season either, creating just nine big chances in the Premier League, the fewest of any team alongside Aston Villa and Coventry, but it clicked in Austria, albeit against weaker opposition.
Bradley Barcola will hope he has ignited his Liverpool career while Florian Wirtz delivered a confidence-boosting performance and Lewis Koumas' goal will help him grow in stature.
Liverpool are still very much a work in progress as Iraola finds a formula to blend his big-money signings with a new style of play.

articles.headline: Earth's "vital signs" pushed to record extremes in 2026, report says
keyFacts: Researchers said in a new report that climate change pushed Earth's vital signs to record extremes in 2026.
The report stated that seven of sixteen climate markers reached record extremes, with carbon dioxide levels higher than in the last two million years.
Researchers warned that faster warming increases the risk of crossing irreversible tipping points and called for rapid emissions reductions.
body: Climate change pushed the Earth's environmental system to, and perhaps beyond, its limits in 2026, as several of its "vital signs" reached record extremes, researchers said in a new report on the state of the global climate.

Of the 16 climate markers that researchers consider integral measures of how the Earth is doing, seven are currently at record extremes, while multiple others show evidence of accelerating or abruptly shifting, the report published Wednesday in the peer-reviewed journal BioScience said.

The markers include greenhouse gases, temperature, glacier mass, oceans, wildfires and the planet's energy imbalance, which refers to the difference between the amount of energy the Earth absorbs and the amount it radiates back out into the atmosphere.
Researchers warned in the report that the planet's climate "is moving deeper into uncharted territory."

"Earth's life-support systems are being pushed beyond stable limits, with changes unfolding faster than our ability to respond," the report said. "Across the globe, extreme heat, floods, droughts, storms, and wildfires are no longer rare events but defining features of a changing planet."
A record year
July 2026 broke records as for the contiguous United States, while the country as a whole was experiencing what turned out to be it had ever seen.

Globally, ocean temperatures also reached new heights in July, the report said, while data show that carbon dioxide levels in the atmosphere are higher now than at any other time in the last 2 million years. Heat waves , killing an estimated 14,000, and baked portions of the U.S., too, fueling wildfires that burned millions of acres of land.

Climate change appears to be accelerating, and its effects are becoming more intense, the researchers warned. They noted that the patterns they'd observed while compiling the report had raised concerns about their potential to cross a point of no return, one at which their impacts on various ecosystems would be irreversible.
In 2025, coral reefs became the first environmental system on Earth to reach with researchers saying the damage could be permanent.

Global warming is happening more quickly now than it was a few decades ago, according to the new climate report, which said the rate of warming has sped up, increasing from roughly 0.05 degrees Celsius per decade between 1880 and 1970, to 0.19 degrees Celsius per decade between 1970 and 2010, and 0.36 degrees Celsius per decade between 2010 and 2024.
"Rapid destabilization"

Faster warming increases the likelihood of crossing tipping points from which different environments can't bounce back, and it also risks destabilizing the delicate balance between them, researchers said.

For example, greenhouse gas emissions from , wildfires, or other natural sources, which are all triggered by the temperatures associated with global warming, could essentially become a cycle that fuels itself.

Amplified sea ice loss, ecosystem degradation and carbon emissions could also begin to create their own self-perpetuating feedback loop — the crux of the climate trajectory, where various tipping points act as catalysts that push global warming far past humans' control.
"We are witnessing the rapid destabilization of the Earth's climate system," the researchers said. "This is no longer a warning for the future; it is a diagnosis of the present."

However, the report noted that worsening trends in fossil fuel combustion and other emissions, the main drivers of the extreme changes it centers on, have been accompanied by positive shifts in renewable energy use.
But the researchers emphasized that any progress seen so far "remains far below the scale and speed needed to stabilize Earth's climate system."

"Rapid reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, effective adaptation, ecosystem protection, and transformative societal change remain essential to reducing climate risks and securing a more resilient and sustainable future," they said.
